feedback.solution: The XMP-to-GMP step consumes one ATP per GMP. Two mol GMP therefore consume two mol ATP at this branch step; upstream costs are excluded.

questions.prompt: If 4 mol IMP are directed to AMP, how many mol GTP are consumed at the IMP-to-AMP branch step?

feedback.hint: The adenylosuccinate-forming branch uses GTP.
feedback.solution: The IMP-to-AMP branch uses one GTP per AMP formed. Four mol AMP therefore consume four mol GTP at this branch step; upstream costs are excluded.

questions.prompt: How is the purine ring assembled during de novo purine synthesis?
options: The ring is built stepwise directly on PRPP, producing IMP as the first complete purine nucleotide.
The entire purine ring is completed as a free base before PRPP is attached.
The purine ring is made from orotate before it is attached to ribose.
The ring is assembled only during DNA polymerization.

feedback.hint: Compare whether the base ring is built on ribose or before it.
feedback.solution: Purine atoms are added stepwise to PRPP; IMP is the first complete purine nucleotide.

questions.prompt: Which statement describes de novo pyrimidine synthesis?
options: The ring is assembled before orotate receives a phosphoribosyl group from PRPP to form OMP and then UMP.
The ring is built directly on PRPP one atom at a time, producing IMP.
The first complete pyrimidine is IMP, which is converted to orotate.
The pyrimidine ring is attached only after conversion to CTP.

feedback.hint: Locate the PRPP-attachment reaction relative to orotate formation.
feedback.solution: Pyrimidine ring construction precedes its attachment to PRPP; orotate is converted to OMP and then UMP.

questions.prompt: Which salvage-enzyme pairing is correct?
options: HGPRT uses PRPP to form IMP from hypoxanthine or GMP from guanine; APRT forms AMP from adenine.
HGPRT converts orotate to UMP; APRT forms CTP from UTP.
HGPRT reduces NDP to dNDP; APRT converts dUMP to dTMP.
Both enzymes create the purine ring de novo from amino acids.

feedback.hint: Salvage reuses free bases; identify the bases handled by the two phosphoribosyltransferases.
feedback.solution: HGPRT salvages hypoxanthine and guanine; APRT salvages adenine. Both use PRPP.

questions.prompt: What is the direct substrate/product transformation catalyzed by ribonucleotide reductase?
options: Ribonucleoside diphosphate (NDP) is reduced to the corresponding deoxyribonucleoside diphosphate (dNDP).
dUMP is converted to dTMP using N10-formyl-THF.
PRPP is converted to ribose 5-phosphate.
IMP is converted to AMP using GTP.

feedback.hint: The enzyme name indicates which sugar chemistry it changes.
feedback.solution: Ribonucleotide reductase reduces NDPs to dNDPs; reducing equivalents are supplied through thioredoxin or glutaredoxin systems.

questions.prompt: Which reaction uses 5,10-methylene-tetrahydrofolate as a one-carbon donor?
options: Thymidylate synthase converts dUMP to dTMP and produces dihydrofolate.
Ribonucleotide reductase converts UDP to dUDP using PRPP.
HGPRT converts hypoxanthine to IMP without a ribose donor.
The IMP-to-AMP branch converts GTP to ATP.

feedback.hint: Distinguish the one-carbon-dependent thymidylate reaction from ribose reduction.
feedback.solution: Thymidylate synthase transfers a one-carbon unit from 5,10-methylene-THF to dUMP to make dTMP; dihydrofolate must then be recycled.

questions.prompt: If 4 mol triacylglycerol are completely hydrolyzed, how many mol fatty acids are released?

questions.prompt: How many mol fatty acyl-CoA are required to esterify the three acyl positions in 3 mol newly synthesized TAG?

questions.prompt: Which enzyme sequence describes canonical adipocyte triacylglycerol lipolysis?
options: ATGL: TAG to DAG; HSL: DAG to MAG; MGL: MAG to glycerol.
LPL: TAG to DAG; CPT1: DAG to MAG; ACC: MAG to glycerol.
HSL: TAG to glycerol in one step; MGL: glycerol to fatty acids.
FAS: TAG to DAG; ACC: DAG to MAG; ATGL: MAG to glycerol.

feedback.hint: Follow the successive removal of one fatty acid at each intracellular hydrolysis step.
feedback.solution: ATGL first hydrolyzes TAG, HSL acts mainly on DAG, and MGL hydrolyzes MAG to glycerol. Each step releases a fatty acid.

questions.prompt: In a simplified fed-versus-fasting model, which statement about adipose TAG mobilization is most accurate?
options: Insulin generally suppresses adipose lipolysis in the fed state, while catecholamine-cAMP/PKA signaling can promote droplet access and lipolysis.
Insulin always activates ATGL and HSL during feeding.
Catecholamines convert glycerol directly into fatty acyl-CoA without lipases.
Fasting inhibits all intracellular lipases and prevents fatty-acid release.

feedback.hint: Compare the storage-favoring fed signal with a mobilization signal.
feedback.solution: Insulin generally suppresses adipose lipolysis, whereas catecholamine signaling can promote PKA-dependent lipid-droplet access and lipase action. Regulation is tissue- and state-dependent.

questions.prompt: How does capillary lipoprotein lipase differ from the ATGL-HSL-MGL sequence?
options: Lipoprotein lipase acts on circulating chylomicron/VLDL TAG at capillaries; ATGL, HSL and MGL mobilize intracellular stored TAG.
Lipoprotein lipase is the final intracellular adipose lipase that releases glycerol from MAG.
ATGL acts only on circulating LDL, whereas lipoprotein lipase acts on lipid droplets.
They are the same enzyme with different names.

feedback.hint: Distinguish a circulating lipoprotein particle from an intracellular lipid droplet.
feedback.solution: Capillary LPL hydrolyzes TAG carried by circulating chylomicrons and VLDL; ATGL, HSL and MGL act sequentially on stored cellular TAG.

questions.prompt: What is a common metabolic fate of glycerol released from adipose TAG?
options: It can travel to liver, be phosphorylated by glycerol kinase to glycerol-3-phosphate and enter metabolism through DHAP.
It is converted directly to acetyl-CoA inside the adipocyte without carbon rearrangement.
It is the substrate that CPT1 imports into mitochondria.
It is converted to NADPH by fatty-acid synthase.

feedback.hint: Trace the three-carbon backbone toward a hepatic gluconeogenic intermediate.
feedback.solution: Glycerol can be carried to liver, phosphorylated to glycerol-3-phosphate and oxidized to DHAP, which can enter gluconeogenesis or glycolysis.

questions.prompt: How does hepatic TAG connect with the lipoprotein route?
options: Hepatocytes can package TAG into VLDL for export; capillary LPL later removes TAG from circulating VLDL.
Hepatocytes package TAG only into intestinal chylomicrons containing ApoB-48.
VLDL is synthesized in adipose lipid droplets and hydrolyzed by mitochondrial ATGL.
TAG cannot leave the liver because it is water soluble.

feedback.hint: Connect the intracellular hepatic storage-lipid pool to the liver-derived circulating particle.
feedback.solution: Liver-derived TAG is packaged into VLDL. In circulation, capillary LPL hydrolyzes VLDL TAG and releases fatty acids to tissues.

The citrate pool doubled in size because M+3 increased by five percentage points.
Pyruvate dehydrogenase stopped because the M+0 fraction fell.

21.5 ATP-equivalents because acetoacetate oxidation produces the extra NADH.

questions.prompt: Which statement best distinguishes canonical hepatic ketolysis from a reported alternative ketone-carbon fate?

Canonical oxidative ketolysis uses SCOT; a mouse hepatocyte study reported SCOT-independent ketone-carbon incorporation into lipids, which is a different anabolic fate and does not establish ATP-producing ketolysis.
Human liver tissue studies show that every liver cell expresses SCOT and uses ketones as its preferred respiratory fuel.
SCOT-independent lipid labeling proves that ketones sustain hepatic ATP production through the TCA cycle.

feedback.solution: Mature hepatocytes generally lack SCOT-mediated oxidative ketolysis. A mouse study reported SCOT-independent incorporation of ketone carbon into lipids; that anabolic result does not demonstrate canonical ATP-producing ketolysis.

questions.prompt: A synthetic tracer model assigns 8.0% of lipogenic acetyl-CoA in preadipocytes and 26.0% in differentiated adipocytes to branched-chain amino-acid carbon. What is the absolute change?

3.25 percentage points.
No change can be calculated.

The result proves that leucine carbon supplies net glucose in all mammalian tissues.
The measured share is a universal rate of BCAA oxidation in humans.

questions.prompt: What can the synthetic M+0/M+1/M+2 ribose distribution establish by itself?

It proves that every ribose carbon came from glucose and excludes unlabeled inputs.

The whole-body cholesterol pool is balanced because the four stated rates are nonzero.

No ATP is being synthesized or consumed.
Oxygen consumption and every pathway flux must be zero.
The ATP concentration is known without the compartment volume.
